newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices steady to lower.

text.p: U.S. millfeed prices were steady to mostly lower on Wednesday in a featureless spot market, several dealers said.
"It is dead. People are still harvesting in the Dakotas and Minnesota, so they are not worried about feed business right now, a Kansas dealer said.
Kansas City spot prices dropped one dollar to bid at $97.00 a ton and offer at $99.00.
Spot Kansas/Oklahoma interior values also slipped one dollar to offer at $112 a ton.
"It is mid-week and people have not gotten serious about pricing yet," a broker said. "It is not a priority right now."
Business was also slow in Minnesota as buyers wait for lower prices, a Minnesota dealer said. But the cold weather forecast for the upper Midwest may increase feed usage, he noted.
Everything continues about the same, a Buffalo dealer said. "No extra run time by the Northeastern mills keeps the nearby markets pretty snug," he added.
In the Carolinas, nearby prices remained firm. It appeared some merchants were short in the market and mills remained on reduced times.
"They (merchants) are not able to get their needs out of the flour mills so they are trading between each other trying to get their sales," he said.
